blocks.title: Validation of Remediation and Reporting comparison
Validation of Remediation and Reporting exam shortcuts
items: Patch installed, need automated confirmation → RESCAN
Run the scanner again to ensure the finding is resolved.
Example: A post-patch scan no longer detects the CVE.
Need manual proof the control works → VERIFICATION
Example: Confirm the vulnerable service no longer accepts the exploit path.
Need evidence process was followed → AUDIT
Review records, approvals, and control evidence.
Example: An auditor checks patch records and exception approvals.
Need to communicate status and residual risk → REPORTING
Summarize what was found, what changed, and what remains.
Example: Leadership receives a remediation dashboard.
blocks.example: Focus on which stage of the vulnerability-management lifecycle the scenario is describing.

questions.q: After patching a server, the security team runs the vulnerability scanner again to confirm the finding is gone. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Rescanning repeats the automated assessment after remediation.

questions.q: A security engineer manually tests the previously vulnerable function to confirm the fix actually works. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Verification directly confirms the remediation works as intended.

questions.q: An auditor reviews patch records, exception approvals, and remediation evidence. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: An audit reviews evidence and process compliance.

questions.q: Leadership receives a dashboard showing open vulnerabilities, remediation progress, and residual risk. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Reporting communicates vulnerability status and outcomes to stakeholders.
